beat.title: 7. The Witness (Certificate) Protocol V(x, w)
beat.question: How does a mathematical verifier prove an answer without doing the hard search?
beat.insight: A verifier V(x, w) runs in polynomial time, returning YES if and only if certificate w proves instance x has a YES answer.

context.answer: A polynomial-time verifier V(x, w) is a deterministic checker that takes a problem instance x and a short proof certificate (witness) w, and confirms in O(n^k) steps whether w is a valid solution for x. Instead of searching through 2^n possibilities from scratch, the verifier only checks one proposed witness and outputs YES if and only if every constraint passes.
